learning_units.description: Circumambulation timing drill around the kalam boundary.

social_formats.description: Solo ritual performer enacting stories and circumambulating in front of temple audience and drum ensemble.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Hand gestures in Koothu derived from Kathakali/Koodiyattam idioms; wielding small sword in right hand during oracle phase
movement_profile.footwork: Slow circular walking steps escalating into fast running strides and floor-smearing sweeps
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Circular spatial path around the floor kalam, terminating inside the artwork boundary
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Minimal torso rotation during narrative phase, dynamic full-body shifting during kalam erasure
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Ground-level stepping with sudden leaps into the center of the kalam
movement_profile.partnering: Solo dancer interacting with sacred objects, lamp, and floor artwork
movement_profile.posture: Upright torso during circumambulation; energetic, loose-framed trance posture during frenzy phase

signature_moves.description: Making 9 or 11 measured circular passes around the painted floor diagram.
signature_moves.name: Kalam Circumambulation

signature_moves.description: Leaping into the painted figure and smearing the sacred powders with both feet and right hand.
signature_moves.name: Kalam Erasing

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Gradual building from solemn slow walk to wild accelerating frenzy
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Do not perform secular commercial adaptations or alter sacred ritual sequences.

music_profile.meter: Flexible metric cycles changing from slow devotional invocations to rapid drum pulses
music_profile.musical_form: Sequential ritual structure: invocatory songs (Kottum Pattum), narrative Thottam recitation, drum accompaniment to Koothu, and accelerating trance percussion for Velichchappaadu
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Accelerating circular beats driven by chenda, para, and ilathalam
music_profile.sound_description: Resonant, deep drum beats from para and chenda interspersed with the bright metallic clatter of ilathalam cymbals, accompanied by archaic vocal chants in Sopanam ragas.
music_profile.tempo_bpm: 60-160 BPM accelerating over the course of ritual phases
music_profile.vocal_style: Stylized vocal recitation in old Malayalam and Tamil, Sopanam style and Carnatic ragas

basic_steps: Circumambulation (slow walking along the outer perimeter of the sacred kalam)
Tempo acceleration step (gradual shortening of stride while increasing pace around the kalam)
Frenzy leap (stepping directly into the ritual ground painting at peak tempo)
Foot erasure sweep (using both legs to smear and erase the body section of the powder painting)
Hand erasure stroke (using the right hand to erase the facial section of the sacred figure)
teaching.formation: Circular spatial path circumambulating the ground kalam in front of a lighted lamp
teaching.level_notes: Ritual performance restricted to hereditary community initiates.
teaching.rhythm: Accelerating rhythmic drum cycles played on chenda and para with ilathalam cymbals
